quests.contextSentence: The woman who runs the pharmacy remembered my name.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'who' is a relative pronoun for people. It points back to the woman, since she is the one who runs the pharmacy.
quests.nativeTip: 'Who' points to a person. Which noun runs something?

quests.contextSentence: The recruiter phoned the candidates who had missed the first interview.
quests.ruleExplanation: The relative clause 'who had missed the first interview' describes the candidates. The recruiter is the one phoning, not the one who missed it.

quests.contextSentence: Visitors who park behind the annex must register at the office.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' introduces information about people, so it points to visitors. The annex and the office are places.
quests.nativeTip: Who parks, and who has to register?

quests.contextSentence: The printer on the second floor, which jams constantly, is being replaced by facilities.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' refers to a thing and is set off by commas. The printer is the thing that jams, not the floor or the department.

quests.contextSentence: The hotel offers free breakfast, which most guests skip.
quests.ruleExplanation: The 'which' clause comments on the noun directly before it. Guests skip the breakfast, not the hotel or themselves.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'which' points back to ➔ 'the free breakfast'

quests.contextSentence: The lease, which the housing association amended in March, now allows pets.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'which' refers to the thing described by the clause. The housing association did the amending, and the lease was the thing changed.

quests.contextSentence: The email that Joanna sent yesterday contained the wrong attachment.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' is the object of 'sent' inside the clause. It stands for the email that Joanna sent.

quests.contextSentence: Please return the books that you borrowed from the library before the holidays.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' refers to the items borrowed. The library is where they came from, and the holidays are only a time.

quests.contextSentence: The app that my daughter installed on the family tablet keeps freezing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That my daughter installed' describes which app. The tablet is where it is installed, not the thing installed.

quests.contextSentence: Dr. Menon, whose clinic opens at eight, has already left home.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'whose' shows possession and points to the owner. The clinic belongs to Dr. Menon.

quests.contextSentence: The tenants whose flats face the road complained about the noise.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'whose' points to the possessor, the tenants, and 'flats' is the thing possessed. The road is just what the flats face.

quests.contextSentence: The company whose software crashed during the demo lost the contract.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whose' introduces the owner of the software. That is the company, not the demo where the crash happened.

quests.contextSentence: The candidate whom the panel interviewed first withdrew from the process.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'whom' is the object of 'interviewed'. The panel did the interviewing, so 'whom' is the candidate.

quests.contextSentence: My cousin, with whom I share a flat, works nights.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whom' follows the preposition 'with' and replaces a person. The person the speaker shares a flat with is the cousin.

quests.contextSentence: The two nurses to whom the patient handed the form were both new.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To whom' names the receivers. The patient is the giver and the form is what was given, so the nurses are the referent.
quests.nativeTip: To whom was the form handed?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'whom' points back to ➔ 'the two nurses'

quests.contextSentence: The report that the auditors submitted was returned because it lacked signatures.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'that' refers to the thing submitted. The auditors submitted it, and the signatures are what it lacked.

quests.contextSentence: The colleague who covered my shift also fixed the projector, which had been broken for weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'which' follows the noun right before it and refers to a thing. The projector had been broken.

quests.contextSentence: Anyone who has completed the form and the survey can collect a badge, which is valid for one year.
quests.ruleExplanation: The clause after 'which' is about the item just mentioned. It is the badge that can be collected and stays valid.
quests.nativeTip: What is valid for a year?

quests.contextSentence: The manager of the two shops who called us is based in Leeds.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'who' refers to a person and the verb 'called' needs a person subject. So it is the manager, not the closer noun 'the two shops'.

quests.contextSentence: The manual for the new machine, which is written in six languages, is on the shelf.
quests.ruleExplanation: A manual is written in languages, whereas a machine is not. So 'which' refers to the manual despite the closer noun.
quests.nativeTip: What can be written in a language?

quests.contextSentence: The teacher of the class, who trained in Nairobi, lives near me.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' needs a person. A class is a group of learners here, and the person who trained is the teacher.

quests.contextSentence: The proposal that Mr. Ito rejected on behalf of the committee has been resubmitted.
quests.ruleExplanation: Consider the form of 'that': it is the object of 'rejected'. The proposal is what was turned down and then resubmitted.

quests.contextSentence: The customer, whom the agent had promised a refund, was still waiting.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'whom' is the receiver of the promise. The agent promised, the refund was promised, and the customer was the one promised to.

quests.contextSentence: My neighbours, whose dog barks all night, have promised to move it indoors.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'whose' points back to the owner. The dog belongs to the neighbours, who are the people making the promise.

quests.contextSentence: The council has approved a scheme that will fund new cycle lanes across the city.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' begins a clause about the scheme. It is the scheme that will fund the lanes, not the council itself.
quests.nativeTip: What will fund the cycle lanes?

quests.contextSentence: The charger, which weighs less than a phone, comes with a travel case.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which weighs less than a phone' describes the charger. The phone is only used for comparison.
quests.nativeTip: What weighs less than a phone?

quests.contextSentence: Officials confirmed that the two suspects, whom police had questioned twice, were released without charge.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whom' is the object of 'questioned'. The police did the questioning, so 'whom' is the two suspects.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'whom' points back to ➔ 'the two suspects'

quests.contextSentence: The clerk who served us couldn't find the receipt that we had kept, so he asked us to fill in a form.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That we had kept' describes the receipt. The clerk is described by 'who', and the form is added later.

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Anand, whose team launched the app that crashed on day one, apologised herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That crashed on day one' describes the app the team launched. The team and Ms. Anand did not crash.

quests.contextSentence: The neighbours, whom the caretaker had warned twice, finally fixed the gate that their children had broken.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'whom' is the object of 'warned'. The caretaker gave the warnings, so the warned people are the neighbours.
